source.section: Appendix C Creative banks and exact treatment addressing

count_contract: There are 240 underlying premises, 120 learning and 120 fiction, and 2,400 addressable candidate treatments. There were zero independently written complete treatment scripts, zero catalogue recipe renders and zero audience studies in that catalogue. Factual checkability is not factual verification. Lexically distinct ideas are not proven novel against all historical work. Select one premise for a concrete viewer task, resolve its facts and rights, write an actual storyboard and test its risky action.

F01.structure: A question, visible cause, resulting change, bounded takeaway.
F01.gate: Show a single causal chain and state model limits.

F02.structure: Setup, fair question, quiet thinking beat, result, explanation.
F02.gate: Do not use guessing to teach emergency response.

F03.structure: A concrete starting state, two or three decisions, checked outcome.
F03.gate: Verify every instructional step against the chosen source.

F04.structure: Matched conditions, one stated difference, observed consequence.
F04.gate: Counterfactual outcomes remain hypotheses until validated.

F05.structure: Show an outcome, inspect clues backward, replay the verified chain.
F05.gate: Sequence must support causality rather than merely correlation.

F06.structure: A want, obstacle, choice, consequence and closing image.
F06.gate: A lesson is a theme, not evidence for a general factual claim.

F07.structure: The protagonist faces two costs and commits to one path.
F07.gate: Both branches must be plausible within the established world.

F08.structure: The viewer sees a clue the character misses until the payoff.
F08.gate: Stage clues fairly and avoid a hidden last-second solution.

F09.structure: A simple task escalates through linked attempts and resolves.
F09.gate: Every gag should follow from the previous action.

F10.structure: Retell a causal scene from a prop or helper's perspective.
F10.gate: Change information and emphasis, not merely narration wording.

F11.structure: A finished original composition separates into actual useful layers.
F11.gate: Only use source layers that really exist.

F12.structure: A traveler crosses a coherent miniature environment.
F12.gate: Preserve scale, route continuity and contact.

F13.structure: Progressive sourced visual clues lead to one defensible answer.
F13.gate: Use verified place identity and rights-cleared imagery.

F14.structure: A symptom, diagnostic check, change and rechecked result.
F14.gate: Distinguish observed repair from proposed fix.

F15.structure: A bounded claim is tested and its exceptions are explained.
F15.gate: Requires primary evidence; do not invent a popular myth.

F16.structure: Original audio establishes a pattern that visual action transforms.
F16.gate: Rights, accessibility and mix are separate checks.

F17.structure: A recurring prop appears in genuinely different original conflicts.
F17.gate: Each episode needs its own premise and resolution.

F18.structure: A modeled object is assembled, rotated and checked.
F18.gate: Distinguish illustrative assembly from safe build instructions.

F19.structure: A sourced dataset answers a bounded question with visible units.
F19.gate: Check denominator, scope, date and interpolation.

F20.structure: The same mechanism alternates between schematic and tangible views.
F20.gate: Keep correspondences exact and disclose simplifications.

A01.construction: Use original articulated line characters, crisp props and explicit highlights. Keep one causal relationship legible at a time.
A01.communicative_difference: Emphasizes symbolic relationships, exact matching and readable cause/effect without depth distractions.
A01.gate: Rig contacts, text layout and every diagram relationship must be checked; this is 2D animation.

A02.construction: Stage the same action as a drawn field-note sequence. Add traces, section views and short observations in the order they are needed.
A02.communicative_difference: Makes reasoning and uncertainty visible through progressive construction, rather than presenting only the final state.
A02.gate: Verify stroke order, annotation tracking and model limits. Rough strokes must never change factual geometry.

A03.construction: Build the scene with original volumetric props and grounded characters, then use lighting, contact and a restrained camera to show the same conflict.
A03.communicative_difference: Emphasizes embodied effort, occlusion and spatial consequences that the diagrammatic view abstracts.
A03.gate: Requires a real 3D scene, alternate-angle check, contact/shadow review and source reopening. Blockbench is a research-only asset option.

A04.construction: Create original foreground, character, prop and background planes with meaningful depth order. Use gentle parallax, grounded articulation and explicit masks to stage the existing story.
A04.communicative_difference: Emphasizes layered attention, a rich setting and a gradual foreground/background discovery while retaining the readability of illustration.
A04.gate: This is 2.5D, not true volumetric 3D. Check masks, disocclusion gaps, foot anchors, occlusion order, scene-space transforms and every texture license.

I01.first_frame: A toppled original prop fills the frame.
I01.action: Hold briefly, trace back to the initiating contact.

I02.first_frame: The same simple setup appears left and right.
I02.action: Both begin together; a single changed parameter is highlighted.
I02.sound: Shared pulse with separate result accents.

I03.first_frame: A small character crosses a richly rendered scene toward an obstacle.
I03.action: Camera tracks at walking speed and settles before the decision.

I04.first_frame: An honest silhouette appears on a textured stage.
I04.action: Light rotates slowly while the camera stays fixed.

I05.first_frame: A complete scene is visible immediately.
I05.action: Two meaningful layers peel apart without hiding the subject.

I06.first_frame: A distinctive token begins at the first node of a network.
I06.action: Track it through one junction, then pause before the next.
I06.sound: Single pluck at each verified handoff.

I07.first_frame: A character enters carrying an absurdly oversized tool.
I07.action: Their confident step stops at the tiny problem.
I07.text_seed: There may be an easier way.
I07.sound: Small comic stop and room tone.

I08.first_frame: A physical indicator or step result is framed clearly.
I08.action: Pull back to show the action it checks.
I08.text_seed: How would you know it worked?
I08.sound: Neutral click matched to the indicator.

I09.first_frame: A sourced warning cue is visible in an otherwise calm scene.
I09.action: A bounded highlight draws attention, then stops.

I10.first_frame: A fictional route is shown as a clean map.
I10.action: Dissolve to the same route in an original miniature scene.
I10.text_seed: The map leaves out one thing.

I11.first_frame: The scene and two options are already legible.
I11.action: A gentle progress bar begins after the rule appears.
I11.sound: Soft regular ticks, optional silent mode.

I12.first_frame: An object sits with one clearly empty socket.
I12.action: A slow turn reveals the gap from a second view.

I13.first_frame: An original tap is paired with a visible waveform.
I13.action: The waveform settles into the moving object that made the sound.

I14.first_frame: A character steps out from behind an actual scene edge.
I14.action: Camera holds while they discover the central prop.
I14.sound: Footstep, breath and small music motif.

I15.first_frame: A circular everyday object fills the screen.
I15.action: Match cut to a different-scale system with the same silhouette.

I16.first_frame: The external object is visible against a calm background.
I16.action: A cutaway plane opens to show the interacting parts.

I17.first_frame: Three repeated actions establish a visual rhythm.
I17.action: A fourth object breaks one stated rule.
I17.sound: Three even taps and a held rest.

I18.first_frame: A final object rests beside three traces of its journey.
I18.action: The camera follows the traces backward without reversing physics.
I18.sound: Music starts on the resolved chord then thins.

I19.first_frame: Two characters look at the same object from different sides.
I19.action: A small orbit reveals why each saw something different.
I19.text_seed: They both saw part of it.
I19.sound: Two short vocal reactions, optional captions.

I20.first_frame: A tool begins one approved, safe action.
I20.action: The title arrives in empty space after the action is recognizable.
I20.sound: Real or original matched tool sound.

I21.first_frame: An obstruction dominates near frame while the goal remains visible.
I21.action: Slow lateral move reveals a plausible path.
I21.sound: Ambient sound with one discovery accent.

I22.first_frame: A simple shape is drawn around the key object.
I22.action: The outline becomes a guide for the later explanation.

I23.first_frame: A tiny character stands beside a large, grounded object.
I23.action: Wide shot holds before a closer insert of their tool.

I24.first_frame: An authentic capture or labeled mockup opens at a known state.
I24.action: One highlight indicates the next action, not a fake cursor success.
I24.sound: Clear spoken step and quiet click.

I25.first_frame: Three dated or explicitly fictional time panels sit together.
I25.action: The middle panel expands into the main scene.

I26.first_frame: The central action sits low in a spacious scene.
I26.action: A short question appears above without covering evidence.

I27.first_frame: Two objects are just about to touch.
I27.action: A character interrupts at the last moment and creates a new problem.
I27.sound: Held note and soft comic release.

I28.first_frame: A character demonstrates the fictional rule once in plain view.
I28.action: A second attempt introduces the conflict.

I29.first_frame: A real or clearly simulated failed result sits beside a corrected proposal.
I29.action: Camera moves to the single changed region.

I30.first_frame: A foreground character starts a solitary task.
I30.action: Slow push keeps a helpful background action visible.
I30.sound: Gentle ambient music, no forced crescendo.

M01.mechanism: A slow, continuous move toward the causal detail.
M01.check: Keep essential evidence and text in safe areas.

M02.mechanism: Move sideways to uncover an occluded relationship.
M02.check: Use consistent geometry or disclose a 2.5D approximation.

M03.mechanism: Hold the camera while meaningful objects move.
M03.check: The frame may be calm; the action must remain legible.

M04.mechanism: Track one identified object through a system.
M04.check: Maintain identity through every cut and occlusion.

M05.mechanism: Look down at a sequence of workstations or steps.
M05.check: Do not obscure contact points with labels.

M06.mechanism: Rotate around an object far enough to reveal a hidden side.
M06.check: Requires true 3D or genuine alternate views.

M07.mechanism: Move a section plane while the object stays fixed.
M07.check: Plane position must agree with visible parts.

M08.mechanism: Separate related parts along meaningful axes.
M08.check: Keep connectors and parent-child relationships clear.

M09.mechanism: Synchronize two views to a shared time authority.
M09.check: Check identical starting state and duration.

M10.mechanism: Step through explicit scales with reference objects.
M10.check: Show units and avoid arbitrary size jumps.

M11.mechanism: Move background, characters, shadows and targets together.
M11.check: Apply one shared transform and its inverse.

M12.mechanism: Move declared foreground and background planes differently.
M12.check: Inspect disocclusion gaps and do not call it metric 3D.

M13.mechanism: Shift emphasis from cause to effect through motion and light.
M13.check: Keep both visible long enough to establish their relationship.

M14.mechanism: A character shifts weight before the main action.
M14.check: Anchor the planted foot and use coherent mass transfer.

M15.mechanism: A moving prop passes its target slightly and settles.
M15.check: Use controlled easing; avoid implying real damping data.

M16.mechanism: Slow or hold immediately before the meaningful choice.
M16.check: Hold after the viewer has all necessary information.

M17.mechanism: Leave a fading trace of an object's path.
M17.check: Separate history from simultaneous object copies.

M18.mechanism: Move the free degrees of freedom while anchors stay fixed.
M18.check: Check constraints numerically before claiming fidelity.

M19.mechanism: A secondary part moves against the primary mass.
M19.check: Keep joints and inertia narratively or physically coherent.

M20.mechanism: Show multiple labeled moments in a consistent composition.
M20.check: Label time and avoid implying all states coexist.

M21.mechanism: Visit earlier states in order with explicit time labels.
M21.check: Do not reverse the direction of a real process without a label.

M22.mechanism: Move at the character's height along their route.
M22.check: Establish environment and avoid disorienting fast pans.

M23.mechanism: Transition between plan view and embodied perspective.
M23.check: Keep landmarks matched and use a true scene when claiming 3D.

M24.mechanism: Expose an object through a controlled, fair mask.
M24.check: Check no unintended answer leaks or impossible ambiguity.

M25.mechanism: Trace the actual contour or route in ordered segments.
M25.check: Stroke order must match the explanation.

M26.mechanism: One restrained pulse marks the input before motion propagates.
M26.check: Never substitute flashing for a meaningful relationship.

M27.mechanism: Let a character leave while the consequence stays visible.
M27.check: The final frame must complete the narrative promise.

M28.mechanism: A grounded object passes briefly in front of the subject.
M28.check: Do not hide essential puzzle evidence or a discontinuity.

M29.mechanism: Repeat an action with a new obstacle each time.
M29.check: Each repeat changes a causal or narrative condition.

M30.mechanism: Settle into a readable final arrangement and hold.
M30.check: Keep the answer visible long enough and avoid abrupt cutoff.

editorial_rules.F01: F01 explains the relationship through the story's visible action and bounded takeaway.
editorial_rules.F02: F02 asks the story question before a fair thinking hold, then resolves it from visible evidence. It is excluded from the public-safety group.
editorial_rules.F03: F03 separates one worked case into setup, action and a checked checkpoint.
editorial_rules.F04: F04 compares initial and changed conditions while isolating one justified variable; no invented counterfactual result.
editorial_rules.F05: F05 starts at the outcome, inspects clues, then replays the supported chain forward without overstating causality.
editorial_rules.F06: F06 stages a want, obstacle, committed choice, consequence and the authored ending.
editorial_rules.F07: F07 makes the costs of two plausible choices visible; an unexecuted alternate branch stays labeled proposed.
editorial_rules.F08: F08 gives the viewer a fair advance clue before the protagonist notices it; no last-second coincidence.
editorial_rules.F09: F09 lets readable actions and reactions carry the story with sparse captions and purposeful sound.
editorial_rules.F10: F10 retells the same conflict from an existing prop/helper viewpoint without inventing a new solution.
editorial_rules.F20: F20 alternates schematic and tangible representations of one relationship. Practical guidance needs an approved factual script first.

combination_rules.learning: Learning combinations fail if their comparison has no controlled basis, their backward trace overstates causality, or factual verification removes the premise.
combination_rules.fiction: Fiction combinations fail if their alternative choice, advance clue or object viewpoint requires a contrived new premise rather than illuminating the existing one.
combination_rules.every: Every combination inherits the story risks, format gate, approach gate, rights review, caption readability, motion comfort, audio mix and exact-byte checks.
